name: Origen
bio:
Teacher at Alexandria and later at Caesarea in Palestine, the most prolific biblical scholar of the early church; he compiled the Hexapla, a six-column edition of the Old Testament, and was imprisoned and tortured in the persecution under Decius, dying soon after.

His Commentary on John, begun at Alexandria about 231 for his patron Ambrose, is the oldest surviving commentary on that Gospel; of its thirty-two books, nine survive in Greek. Some of his teachings were condemned after his death, and he is not counted among the saints.
